newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan's Jupiter cable operator may boost capital.
newsitem.headline: Japan's Jupiter cable operator may boost capital.

text.p: Cable television operator Jupiter Telecommunications Co will need about 20 billion yen in fresh capital a year over the next few years for investments in optic-fibre networks, a Jupiter official said on Friday.

Jupiter, owned 60 percent by Sumitomo Corp and 40 percent by a Japanese unit of Tele-Communications Inc, would also likely boost its capitalisation from the current 18.5 billion yen next year, he said.
Jupiter aimed to have 140,000 cable television subscribers by the end of December 1997, up from the current 100,000, he said.
A planned telephone service using its cable TV networks -- due to start in Tokyo next July -- also requires substantial investment in exchange systems, he said.

The official declined to comment on details, except to say that the company had in the past relied totally on capitalisation to finance its investment, but might turn to bank borrowings next year. ($1 = 114.8 yen)
